content:
Phase 50: read-only mode — plan submission (round 1). docs/phases/read-only-mode.md on branch phase-50-read-only-mode (46e84fc amended).

Problem: the one-cycle-writing-call rule is enforced by prose only. panel.run_lens sets TAGTEAM_PANEL_LENS but nothing in the package reads it — the panel only detects a stray lens write after the fact (round-log length / seq compare). The codex-brief and verifier agents have Bash and honor-system never-write rules. Arbiter ruled 2026-09-03: enforced read-only mode first; shipping agents in the plugin is a later phase that depends on this one (backlog entry added).

Design: TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1 (process-scoped, env parse in one place). Enforced at the two chokepoints, not a CLI command table: (1) dualwrite.writer_lock raises ReadOnlyError on entry before _ensure_tagteam_dir / lock file / thread lock — nothing touches disk; covers all 29 file+DB write sites. (2) db writer functions guarded by a @_writes decorator, with a source-level test that every db.py function containing INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE is decorated. Alternative considered and not recommended: sqlite ?mode=ro — changes read-path behaviour when the DB is absent (connect creates+migrates today) and surfaces SQLite's error, not ours. cli.py catches ReadOnlyError at the dispatcher: one refusal line, exit 2; read-only commands unchanged (tested). Who sets it: panel lens children yes (post-hoc detection kept); briefer child if its writes are parent-side (confirm in impl, else move them); headless turns NO (tested both ways); Claude Code subagents prefix their own calls (still their choice — but once set, enforced). Contract gains one 'read-only helpers' paragraph in all three copies (byte-identity + vendored-hash tests guard). Out: shipping agents, PreToolUse hook, any change to what headless/watcher/gate may write. Target 3.11.0.

Please rule on the db-guard choice (decorator vs mode=ro) if you disagree; everything else is in the doc (Scope, Files, Done means, Verification plan).

One plan blocker remains: the proposed `db` writer decorators do not cover mutations performed by `db.connect()` itself.

`connect()` currently creates the DB parent directory, opens/creates `tagteam.db`, executes `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, runs every pending schema migration, and commits. Read commands such as `usage`, `brief` (show), and several status paths call `db.connect()`. Therefore `TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1` on a fresh project can create `.tagteam/`, the database, and WAL/SHM files before any decorated writer function is reached; on an older database it can migrate the schema. This contradicts both “nothing touches disk” and the Done criterion that project/DB files remain byte-identical after read-only commands.

Revise the design to define a genuinely non-mutating connection path while `TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY` is set. Using SQLite URI `mode=ro` for an existing database is the direct option (the repository already has a precedent in `hub_api.read_only_connect`); an absent database must be handled without creating it, either by readers falling back to canonical files/empty results or by an explicitly specified in-memory read model. Keep the decorators if desired as the clear refusal mechanism for DB writer APIs, but they cannot substitute for read-only connection semantics.

Extend verification to cover (1) a fresh project with no `.tagteam` directory/DB and (2) an existing current-schema DB with no pre-existing WAL/SHM sidecars, snapshotting the full relevant tree before and after representative read commands. Also cover an old-schema fixture so read-only mode proves it refuses/falls back rather than migrating it.

The decorator choice is otherwise reasonable, and the writer-lock, panel-child environment, briefer-parent bookkeeping, headless exclusion, CLI error handling, and contract-copy portions are well scoped.

Round 2 — blocker accepted: db.connect itself mutates (mkdir, create, WAL pragma, migrate), so the writer decorators were never the read-only guarantee. Design revised in docs/phases/read-only-mode.md, tagged (r2), commit 50fe3c4.

The DB chokepoint is now db.read_only_connect(), and db.connect() delegates to it whenever TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY is set, so all ~70 call sites inherit it without edits: (1) DB absent → DatabaseMissing(ReadOnlyError), nothing created; (2) URI chosen by what is on disk — measured on this machine (SQLite 3.51): with -wal/-shm present, mode=ro honours WAL content (sees a row a still-open writer holds un-checkpointed) and leaves .db and -wal bytes unchanged, though a pre-existing -shm (the WAL index) is rewritten; with NO sidecars, plain mode=ro cannot open a cleanly closed WAL DB at all ('unable to open database file'), while mode=ro&immutable=1 opens it, reads correctly and creates nothing — byte-identical tree; immutable=1 is unsafe only when a -wal exists (it ignores WAL content, measured), which is exactly when we don't use it. Both states occur in the wild: this repo keeps sidecars between commands, ~/projects/QA has only tagteam.db. (3) PRAGMA query_only=ON as the second net. (4) user_version < SCHEMA_VERSION → SchemaBehind(ReadOnlyError), never migrate (newer is allowed per the additive-only rule). Cycle/state/gate-status/panel-status readers already try/except around connect with file fallback — no edits; the three DB-only readers (usage, brief show/list, interject --list) get DatabaseMissing → empty results exit 0, SchemaBehind → refusal exit 2. Decorators kept as the clear refusal for the writer API, not the guarantee. Round-1's 'mode=ro not recommended' is withdrawn.

Found while measuring: hub_api.read_only_connect uses plain mode=ro and so raises on a sidecar-less DB today — it will delegate to the db one (same None/ProjectDataError contract); added to scope.

Verification extended as asked: a tree-snapshot matrix (every path + bytes under the project, before/after each read-only command) over (1) fresh project with no .tagteam — nothing created; (2) current-schema DB with no sidecars — identical, plus the with-sidecars variant where .db and -wal are identical, no file created/removed, -shm allowed to differ; (3) old-schema fixture (_SCHEMA_V1 + user_version=1) — fallback/refusal, user_version still 1, file identical. Plus unit tests for the WAL-visibility property, query_only, and the hub_api fix. 'Done means' now states the one measured -shm exception explicitly.

The original `db.connect()` blocker is substantially addressed, but one connection-state gap remains in the revised plan.

The URI rule currently says “`-wal` **or** `-shm` present → plain `mode=ro`,” while the measured/tested sidecar fixture has both files. A real or crash/interruption state can have `tagteam.db-wal` without `tagteam.db-shm`. In that state SQLite needs a WAL index to read the WAL: plain `mode=ro` can create `tagteam.db-shm` when the directory is writable (or fail when it cannot), which contradicts the new criterion that read-only commands create no file. `immutable=1` is not a fallback because, as the plan correctly notes, it can ignore committed WAL content.

Specify fail-closed behavior for every sidecar combination. A suitable rule is: WAL present + SHM absent → close/refuse with a specific `ReadOnlyError`; WAL + SHM → plain `mode=ro`; no WAL → `immutable=1` (whether a stale SHM exists or not), provided the latter behavior is verified. Another design is acceptable if it both preserves committed WAL content and creates/modifies no unacknowledged file.

Expand the connection and tree-snapshot matrix to cover all four combinations: neither sidecar, WAL+SHM, WAL-only, and SHM-only. For WAL-only, assert either the documented refusal or the chosen safe behavior and assert that no SHM file appears. Clarify whether the documented pre-existing-SHM byte-change exception applies only to WAL+SHM.

Everything else in round 2 resolves the prior feedback: missing and old-schema handling, connection delegation, explicit DB-only-reader behavior, query-only defense, hub reader consolidation, and the expanded scope are sound.

Round 3 — the WAL-only gap accepted and closed with measurements, tagged (r3), commit 4cb5f90.

All four sidecar states measured (SQLite 3.51), this time with a genuine crash state: DB + WAL copied out from under an open writer holding committed frames in the WAL (16 KB), no SHM. Results — neither: mode=ro cannot open, immutable=1 reads and creates nothing. WAL+SHM: mode=ro sees the WAL frames and rewrites the existing -shm; immutable=1 opens but misses the frames. WAL-only: mode=ro reads the frames but CREATES -shm (your prediction, confirmed); immutable=1 misses the frames. SHM-only: mode=ro cannot open; immutable=1 reads the main file and creates/changes nothing.

Rule, exactly as you proposed: WAL+SHM → mode=ro; WAL-only → refuse with WalWithoutIndex(ReadOnlyError) (nothing created, message names the remedy: any normal writing command checkpoints); no WAL (neither, or a stale SHM) → immutable=1, which is now provably unable to hide data because it is used only when no -wal exists. The 0-byte-WAL-only refinement (immutable would be safe there) is deliberately not taken — one more branch for a rare state with a one-command remedy. Clarified: the -shm byte-change exception applies ONLY to the WAL+SHM state; in every other state every file is byte-identical, and no state creates or removes a file.

Verification matrix expanded to all four states with crash-copy fixtures (wal_autocheckpoint=0 under an open writer): WAL-only asserts the refusal for DB-only readers, file fallback for cycle/state readers, and that no -shm appears; SHM-only asserts the stale -shm is untouched. Unit tests for read_only_connect, one per table row. The cycle/state/gate/panel readers' existing try/except fallback covers WalWithoutIndex too — still no edits there; the three DB-only readers map it to the refusal, exit 2.

Approved. The revised plan now handles db.connect itself as the read-only chokepoint and defines safe behavior for every SQLite sidecar state: no-WAL states use immutable mode, WAL+SHM uses mode=ro with the documented SHM-index exception, and WAL-only fails closed without creating SHM or hiding committed WAL frames. Missing and old-schema databases, DB-only readers, file-backed fallbacks, query_only, writer decorators, panel/briefer/headless environment boundaries, hub reader consolidation, contract copies, and the full four-state tree-snapshot matrix are all specified. Ready for implementation.
